correctness.rationale: The Rule 126 bit rule (neighborhood sums 1 or 2 map to 1) and the height h=1,2,4 spatial column-pair transfer construction are specified with labelled spatial origins and temporal wrap. Every closed length-n walk is equivalent to one F_n^h-fixed configuration for every n>=3. Reconstructed the 2^(2h) graph independently from the eight-case rule: its cyclic SCCs are height 1: one singleton loop; height 2: a six-vertex SCC with elementary cycles {4:1,5:2,6:1} plus singleton; height 4: two separate 12-vertex SCCs, each {10:1,11:2,12:1}, the height-2 six-vertex SCC and singleton. Independently enumerated every elementary cycle in those finite graphs and verified a common vertex in each SCC, so the disjoint-cycle determinant expansion gives exactly the claimed P2 and P4 squared; noncyclic components contribute no traces. The trace/determinant formal identity yields all-n counts; divide primitive h=2/h=4 fixed states by periods 2 and 4 (respectively) to obtain b_n/2 and d_n/2. Because 10k..12k are entire intervals, positive combinations cover n>=50 and exclude 49. Strong connectivity and gcd(10,11,12)=1 give Perron growth for P4; analogous gcd(4,5,6)=1 for P2. Finite graph enumeration is a complete certificate of that finite graph, not finite sampling of n. No claim is made for other temporal periods.
